tip: The -ligen ending turns an adjective into an adverb: daglig (daily) becomes dagligen.
Language names are lowercase in Swedish: engelska, not Engelska.
Swedish names people with heta (to be named): heter du means are you named, not do you have.
In Hur gammal är du, du is the only 'you' Swedish needs, from strangers to bosses. Formal Ni is gone.
ta över is a particle verb (take over); the stress falls on the particle över, not on tar.
frysa (to freeze) is a strong verb: present fryser, past frös, with no -de ending.
kommer att plus an infinitive expresses the future: kommer att regna means will rain.
A non-subject first element forces the verb second and the subject third: I princip är vi. Same rule as German and Dutch.
dit means to there for motion; där means there for location. Movement takes dit.
gärna means gladly or willingly; English has no single word for it.
flugit is the supine of flyga (fly); after har it forms the perfect: har flugit.
Add -ut to a compass word for direction: öster plus ut gives österut (eastward).
fler means more for countable things like fler frågor; use mer for uncountable amounts.
ta reda på is a fixed expression meaning to find out; the words stay together.
hoppas is a deponent verb, always keeping the -s: the past is hoppades, never hoppade.
Double definite: "Den nya lägenheten" – article + adjective-a + noun-definite.

target: Vad jag tycker spelar ingen roll.
tip: spela roll means to matter: spelar ingen roll is doesn't matter, literally plays no role.

target: Klockan är fem i halv tre.
english: It is five minutes to half past two.
tip: "Fem i halv tre" = five to half-three = 2:25. Swedish time can be confusing!

target: De föreslog att vi skulle vänta.
english: They suggested that we should wait.
tip: After föreslog att (suggested that), Swedish uses skulle: föreslog att vi skulle vänta.

target: I Stockholm bor det många människor också.
english: In Stockholm live many people too.
tip: "Det" is an expletive (filler) subject. The real subject follows the verb.

target: Bara på sommaren är det så varmt.
english: Only in summer is it this warm.
tip: Seasons take the preposition på: på sommaren means in summer, på vintern in winter.

target: Trevligt att träffas, jag är ny här.
english: Nice to meet you, I'm new here.
tip: 'Ny' (new): en→ny, ett→nytt, definite/plural→nya. The -tt ending marks neuter.

target: Vad fint väder det är idag nog!
english: What lovely weather we're having today!
tip: Exclamation pattern: "Vad" + adjective + noun + "det är"!

english: The project was completed on time.
tip: The -s ending forms a passive: slutfördes means was completed, no extra word for was.

english: In Sweden the summer is short.
tip: Place phrases trigger V2: "I Sverige" (1st) + "är" (2nd) + "sommaren" (3rd).

english: Between the houses there is an alley.
tip: Neuter ett-nouns like hus add no plural ending: ett hus, två hus, definite plural husen.

english: From here you can see the whole city.
tip: man is a generic subject meaning one, you, or people: ser man means you can see.

target: Aldrig har jag sett något sådant.
english: Never have I seen anything like it.
tip: Starting with "aldrig" creates emphasis and triggers V2 inversion.

target: I värsta fall får vi vänta.
english: In the worst case we'll have to wait.
tip: dålig has irregular comparison: dålig, värre, värst; here värsta means worst.

target: Ju mer man övar, desto bättre blir man.
english: The more you practice, the better you get.
tip: ju ... desto ... means the more ... the more: ju mer, desto bättre; both clauses need it.
